analysis.session_summary: The tape was low-conviction: JPY led (+0.462% vs majors) and CHF lagged (-0.501%), with USD/JPY down 56.3 pips and USD/CHF up 38.9 pips. US CPI and UoM surprises stayed inside the noise floor, while the UK GDP beat produced a normal GBP-positive 0.075% impulse. Equities rose (SPX +63.7 points) but VIX also rose to 18.335 (+3.286%) and Brent fell 1.602%, leaving risk tone split. No leg had a single dominant catalyst, so much of the move was flow and technicals.

themes.evidence: JPY mean_vs_majors_pct was 0.462, the highest; USD/JPY closed down 56.3 pips and CHF/JPY down 159.5 pips.
CHF mean_vs_majors_pct was -0.501, the weakest; USD/CHF rose 38.9 pips, EUR/CHF rose 28.8 pips, AUD/CHF rose 35.3 pips, and NZD/CHF rose 31.9 pips.
Core CPI m/m beat produced own_ccy_impulse_pct of 0.008 inside the noise floor; Prelim UoM miss produced 0.029 inside the noise floor.
USD/ZAR fell 563.3 pips while USD/MXN rose 70.6 pips; ZAR strengthened notably, MXN weakened modestly.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD's seven legs were all under 23 pips and none had a clear catalyst; US CPI and UoM only produced short-lived, inside-noise reactions.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD's up leg got a normal UK GDP push (12.7 pips, 47% of the move) but later UoM/Lagarde reactions were muted; the pair closed nearly flat at -0.3 pips.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY's long 1,035-minute down leg of -85.3 pips had Core CPI accounting for only 28% of the move, leaving the rest flow-driven.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF alternated but closed +38.9 pips as a late up leg got 22% from US consumer confidence.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD's 570-minute up leg of +33.0 pips had no clear catalyst and was followed by a -9.8 pip pullback.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD rose on an early 495-minute up leg of +40.2 pips, with only small Iran/CPI/UoM contributions on the later down leg.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD's almost all-day up leg of +66.3 pips had no clear catalyst; a -17.2 pip late pullback trimmed the gain.

polarity_reads.read: The 0.3% vs 0.2% beat produced only a 0.008% USD basket impulse inside the noise floor; despite the surprise, no broad dollar rally, suggesting USD was already positioned for firm inflation or the data did not change the Fed path.
A 0.4% vs 0.0% UK GDP beat produced a normal 0.075% GBP strength impulse; GBP got the expected data bump but it did not dominate the day.
Lagarde produced a muted 0.018% EUR basket impulse, indicating no new policy signal.
A large miss (47.8 vs forecast 51.0) produced only a 0.029% USD basket impulse, implying the market did not translate the sentiment shock into a dollar repricing.
Schlegel's remarks moved the CHF basket only -0.013%, inside noise; no new policy impulse.

scenarios.name: Muted range extension
scenarios.thesis: No high-conviction catalyst emerged; US CPI and UoM were inside noise, UK GDP normal but faded. Majors consolidate within today's ranges, with JPY bid and CHF heavy.
triggers: CAD CPI not yet on tape
scenarios.invalidation: A close beyond today's EUR/USD 53.6-pip range or a clean US CPI follow-through breaks the range.

pair_paths.rationale: Choppy 20-50 pip legs with no clear catalyst; close 1.15996 is 0.56 of range.
Long down leg of -85.3 pips from 01:30 had no single trigger; risk of range before next data.
CHF is the weakest major, but no new catalyst is likely to extend the move beyond today's 49.4-pip range.

scenarios.name: Risk-off carry unwind / JPY extends
scenarios.thesis: Equities rose but VIX also rose, and geopolitical headlines (Iran Supporting Houthis) remain unresolved; a sentiment turn fuels JPY and possibly CHF safe-haven demand, unwinding recent CHF weakness.
scenarios.invalidation: SPX closes above 7670.1 and VIX falls back below 18.335.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's USD/JPY already fell 56.3 pips; a risk-off extension could repeat that magnitude.
If CHF safe-haven demand returns, it can erase today's 38.9-pip rise within the 49.4-pip range.
A risk-off unwind would pressure the high-beta AUD within its 37.2-pip range.

scenarios.name: USD stabilization on Canadian CPI
scenarios.thesis: A soft Canadian CPI headline (forecast -0.1% vs previous 0.5%) or any USD-supportive follow-through from today's muted CPI compresses USD shorts; USD/CAD extends its 45.9-pip up-move.
scenarios.invalidation: CAD CPI at or above 0.0% and USD/CAD reverses below 1.38635.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's USD/CAD rose 45.9 pips; a soft CPI could extend the move.
EUR/USD's close showed -19.8 pips today; a USD bid on data would extend that drift.
USD/CHF already rose 38.9 pips; continued USD strength would support another leg higher.

risks.why_it_matters: USD/CAD already gained 45.9 pips today and sits at 1.38635; the forecast -0.1% vs previous 0.5% invites dovish CAD repricing.
Brent/USD fell 1.602% to 106.774 but VIX rose 3.286% to 18.335; Iran headlines have not been cleanly priced.
Core CPI beat 0.3% vs 0.2% only moved the basket 0.008%; if the dollar cannot rally on firm inflation, USD-bull scenarios fail.
risks.watch: Next US inflation datum and DXY 98.801.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: ECB President Lagarde speaks at 10:00; today her remarks were a muted 0.018% impulse. The main event is the Canadian CPI block at 14:30: headline forecast -0.1% vs previous 0.5%, median 2.0, trimmed 1.9. A soft print can extend USD/CAD's 45.9-pip up day; a firm print can reverse it.
